name: Amazon Sword
description: One of the most iconic aquarium plants in the world. Big, bold leaves that make a dramatic centerpiece. Super forgiving — great for beginners.

name: Java Fern 'Windelov'
description: A lacy, forked variant of Java Fern that looks like it belongs in a fantasy film. Grows slowly, loves low light, and needs no special soil.

name: Java Moss
description: Soft, fluffy, and nearly indestructible. Grows on rocks, driftwood, or anywhere else you put it. Fish and shrimp absolutely love hiding in it.

name: Christmas Moss
description: Branches fan out like a tiny Christmas tree. Gorgeous tied to driftwood, and perfect shelter for baby fish and shrimp.

name: Anubias Nana Petite
description: Tiny, dark, and almost impossible to kill. Attach it to a rock or piece of driftwood and forget about it — it'll thrive.

name: Anubias Nana on Driftwood
description: Pre-attached to driftwood and ready to drop straight into your tank. Zero setup, instant results.

name: Monte Carlo
description: Creates a lush green carpet along the bottom of your tank. Small round leaves, big visual impact. Needs moderate light to spread properly.

name: Ludwigia Natans Super Red
description: Green on top, deep red underneath. Fast-growing stem plant that adds a dramatic splash of color. Easy to trim and replant cuttings.

name: Sagittaria Subulata
description: A grass-like plant that spreads on its own by sending out runners. Creates a natural-looking meadow with zero effort.

name: Dwarf Baby Tears
description: The tiniest aquarium plant on the planet. Creates a stunning bright green carpet — but it's demanding. Needs CO2 injection and strong light.

name: Rotala Macrandra Green
description: Delicate, wispy stems with pale green leaves that catch the light beautifully. Grows fast and fills the background of a tank like a watercolor painting.

name: Vallisneria
description: Long, ribbon-like grass that sways gracefully in the current. One of the oldest aquarium plants around — grows like a weed in a good way.

name: Hornwort
description: One of the fastest-growing plants you can buy. Great for absorbing excess nutrients, outcompeting algae, and giving fish somewhere to hide.

name: Alternanthera Reineckii Mini
description: A vivid red-pink plant that pops against all the green in a tank. Compact and slow-growing — perfect for the midground.

name: Java Fern
description: The classic low-light workhorse. Hardy, slow-growing, and thrives when attached to rocks or driftwood. Works in almost any tank.

name: Cryptocoryne Wendtii
description: Deep green, ruffled leaves that look great as a midground plant. One of the most forgiving crypts — once established it pretty much takes care of itself.

name: Water Wisteria
description: Fast-growing and forgiving with lacy, fernlike leaves. Can be planted in substrate or left floating. One of the best beginner stem plants.

name: Ludwigia Repens
description: Green and red leaves on a fast-growing stem plant. One of the easiest red plants to keep — great for adding color without the difficulty.

name: Red Tiger Lotus
description: A bulb plant that unfurls into dramatic red lily pads. Grows fast and big — trim the surface leaves to keep it bushy and low.

name: Staurogyne Repens
description: A compact, bushy foreground plant with bright green leaves. Stays low and dense without CO2 — though it grows faster with it.

name: Dwarf Hairgrass
description: Creates a beautiful lawn-like carpet of thin bright green blades. Spreads through runners. Looks incredible — especially in a nano tank.

name: Bucephalandra
description: A rare-looking plant with iridescent shimmer on its leaves. Tie it to driftwood or rock — it'll slowly creep and look stunning.

name: Lobelia Cardinalis
description: Bright lime-green leaves with a reddish underside. A versatile midground plant that grows taller in lower light and stays compact in brighter tanks.

name: Rotala Rotundifolia
description: Slender pink-red stems that look like a coral reef when fully grown in. One of the most popular background stem plants in the hobby.

name: Cryptocoryne Parva
description: The smallest Cryptocoryne in the world. Grows incredibly slowly but creates a dense, natural-looking foreground carpet without needing CO2.

name: Rotala Rotundifolia 'Sunset'
description: A color-changing stem plant that shifts from orange to pink to red depending on how much light it gets. Beautiful in groups at the back of the tank.

name: Anubias Stardust Mini
description: A rare variety of Anubias with striking white speckles on its leaves. Incredibly slow-growing and nearly indestructible — a showpiece plant.

name: Bolbitis Difformis Mini
description: Delicate, feathery fronds that look otherworldly underwater. Attach to rocks or driftwood — it'll slowly creep and fill in beautifully.

name: Azolla (Mosquito Fern)
description: A tiny floating plant that covers the surface with a carpet of soft green rosettes. Shades the tank, reduces algae, and fish love to nibble on it.

name: Eleocharis Belem
description: The finest, most hair-like grass in the hobby. Creates an impossibly delicate carpet that looks like silk underwater — but demands CO2 and high light.

name: Bacopa Monnieri
description: One of the most beginner-friendly stem plants in the hobby. Pairs of bright green, rounded leaves grow up a straight stalk. Hardy and forgiving — just give it decent light and it'll fill in the mid or background beautifully.

name: Anacharis
description: A classic bunch plant that's been in fish tanks forever. Feathery bright green stems grow fast, soak up nitrates, and make a great background filler. Super cheap and nearly impossible to kill.

name: Amazon Frogbit
description: A floating plant with round, lily pad-style leaves and dangling white roots. No planting needed — just drop it in. Fish and shrimp love sheltering under it, and it helps block excess light to keep algae down.

name: Cryptocoryne Beckettii
description: One of the most popular crypts in the hobby. Olive-green leaves with a pink-red tint underneath. Hardy, slow-growing, and thrives in low light — a classic choice for low-tech tanks.

name: Cryptocoryne Lutea
description: A bright yellow-green crypt with gently wavy, oblong leaves. Stays a manageable mid-height — not too small, not too tall. Handles most water conditions without complaining.

name: Hydrocotyle Tripartita
description: One of the trendiest plants in the hobby right now. Tiny clover-shaped leaves carpet the foreground or climb up rocks and wood in a lush, coin-shaped wave. Looks incredible in aquascapes — adds real character.

name: Pogostemon Helferi
description: Also called 'Downoi' (Thai for little star). Short, crinkly leaves fan out in a star-like pattern and form a dense foreground clump. One of the most distinctive-looking plants you can put in a tank.

name: Aponogeton Crispus
description: Grows from a bulb so it's easy to plant — just press it into the substrate. Long, ruffled leaves fan out elegantly and fill background space. Goes dormant occasionally, which is normal, and comes back stronger.

name: Blyxa Japonica
description: A grass-like midground plant with a softer, more natural look than typical stem plants. Popular in nature-style aquascapes for the way its fine leaves sway in the current. Pairs beautifully with stones and driftwood.

name: Rotala Indica
description: A pink-tinged stem plant that's a step up from the basics. Adapts to most conditions and rewards better light and CO2 with deeper, warmer color. Often confused with Rotala Rotundifolia but grows slightly differently.

name: Proserpinaca Palustris
description: Called Mermaid Weed for its fine, saw-toothed leaves that look almost feathery underwater. Color shifts from green to vivid orange-red depending on light and nutrients. A showstopper in well-lit setups.

name: Limnophila Aromatica
description: A compact stem plant with small leaves alternating up the stalk. Develops pink and purple hues under brighter light, adding warm color to the mid or background. Easy to propagate — snip and replant.

name: Fissidens Fontanus
description: Also called Phoenix Moss. Denser and more textured than Java Moss, with feathery fronds that look stunning when tied to rocks and driftwood. Creates a lush, forest-floor look that aquascapers love.

name: Glossostigma Elatinoides
description: A New Zealand native and one of the classic carpet plants in the hobby. Tiny round leaves hug the substrate and form a vivid green lawn effect. Needs high light and CO2 to really take off — but the result is stunning.

name: Utricularia Graminifolia
description: UG is the carpet plant of choice for serious aquascapers. Fine, grass-like blades create a natural meadow look. Fun fact: it's technically carnivorous — tiny bladders catch microscopic organisms in the water.

name: Ammannia Senegalensis
description: Known as Copper Leaf Ammania for its orange-red foliage that glows under intense light. Adds warmth and drama to the background of high-tech tanks. A bold color statement for experienced planted tank keepers.
